figures.note: Mathematical Specification §§2–4, 13; normalization follows clamping. Default untransformed error channels shown.
figures.caption: APGI access schematic. Independently referenced prediction errors are weighted by relative effective gains, centered as excess magnitudes, and integrated over time. The access gate compares the accumulated state with the effective allostatic threshold; cost and expected information value influence threshold dynamics. This is a model schematic, not empirical evidence.

figures.note: Mathematical Specification §§2–4, 13; normalization follows clamping. Default untransformed error channels shown.
figures.caption: The canonical processing sequence separates causal reference standardization, effective-gain clamping and normalization, excess-surprise drive, leaky accumulation, and ignition. The somatic marker amplifies the interoceptive gain; it does not multiply the exteroceptive channel. The displayed excess-magnitude formula is the default untransformed case; the optional Ψ transform requires its own baseline centering.

figures.note: Paper 1 Fig 2 / Paper 2 Fig 2; arrows specify proposed functional interactions.
figures.caption: Proposed vmPFC–VIP⁺–SST⁺ disinhibition pathway. Marker retrieval excites VIP⁺ interneurons, suppressing SST⁺ inhibition and thereby disinhibiting pyramidal dendrites. This proposed physiological implementation requires causal circuit dissociation; it is not established by the schematic.

figures.note: Paper 1 §4.6; Paper 4 Fig 1. Standard-state ATP conversion; κ and whole-event erasure ratio are distinct.
figures.caption: Independent event-energy accounting gives approximately 2.4×10¹⁸ ATP, or 0.12 J under the standard-state ATP conversion. The uncalibrated κ bridge measures ATP per bit of ignition-event information. Full-reset and partial-reset erased-state counts belong to a separate Landauer consistency calculation and must not replace the κ denominator.

figures.note: Paper 1 Fig 2 / Paper 2 Fig 2; arrows specify proposed functional interactions.
figures.caption: Proposed cortical implementation of precision gain. The vmPFC–VIP⁺–SST⁺ pathway is situated alongside laminar input/output routes. Apical–basal plateau and burst physiology does not by itself demonstrate the hypothesized prediction-error computation.

figures.note: Π ≤ 10; γsig is not behavioral Weibull shape k. This hysteresis is not a result from the full reservoir model.
figures.caption: Reduced sigmoid fixed-point model and precision-dependent ignition. The first plotted fold is set to 0.95 by coordinate rescaling; the second lies near 1.02. Curves on the right hold intrinsic γsig=4 and vary Π within its canonical ceiling of 10; their error-referred slopes are not behavioral Weibull αpsy. The reduced-model hysteresis is not a full-reservoir validation result.

figures.note: Illustrative masking model with fixed reference gain; critical ISIs require empirical calibration.
figures.caption: Masking trajectories and parameter sensitivity recomputed from the supplied homogeneous reduced model. The fixed reference gain places the critical ISI near 89.75 ms; increasing target precision shortens it, whereas threshold and spectral-radius changes can lengthen it. No crossing within the search range remains missing. Quantitative ISIs require empirical calibration.

figures.note: Paper 3 §2.1: nesting is computational, not literal anatomy; operational windows are not the OU spectral poles.
figures.caption: Five nested functional levels, with L0 as a reflexive sub-APGI substrate and L1–L4 as progressively slower functional strata. Operational windows are separate from the conditional geometric OU poles. Slow endocrine priors set cortical thresholds rather than acting as spiking ignition reservoirs.

figures.note: Equal stationary variance; geometric poles are conditional model assumptions, not measured neural timescales.
figures.caption: Analytical spectrum from five equal-stationary-variance OU components with τ₀=50 ms and ratio 133. The five-level sum and the L0–L2 partial sum are shown; fitted slopes are approximately −1.01 and −1.00 on their labeled bands, with roughly 5.1 dB ripple for the full sum. Shading denotes the 0.005–100-Hz DC-coupled acquisition band. Poles are conditional model assumptions, not observed timescales.

figures.note: Paper 3 §3 / Fig 3. Subscripted coupling κ differs from the ATP/bit bridge κ.
figures.caption: Proposed fast ACC–LC and slow PVN–HPA influences on lower-level processing. LC is a relay rather than a hierarchical stratum; rapid membrane-MR and sustained GR effects are distinguished. Effective α31 and α41 influences are products of nearest-neighbor κ couplings and are unrelated to the ATP/bit κ bridge.

figures.note: Paper 3: AUC ≥0.75, within-site label permutations, ΔAUC ≥0.05 beyond generic EEG features with BCa CI excluding zero.
figures.caption: Hypothesized psychiatric and clinical profiles with explicit specificity requirements. Major-depression interoceptive precision changes are located at L1; schizophrenia L2 precision is genotype-dependent. Clinical profiling requires the registered permutation and generic-EEG controls; the DoC prognostic study is not evidence for a validated diagnostic classifier.

Patients have CRS-R follow-up at 3 and 6 months and secondary GOS-E at 6 months. Primary Pred 7.G is the baseline-HEP prediction of 3-month CRS-R; the joint HEP+PCI model is estimation-first.

figures.note: Step heights and ages are illustrative; the testable ordering is L2 → L3 → L4. Not the EEG aperiodic exponent.
figures.caption: Illustrative developmental trajectory of detection-series DFA α, not the EEG aperiodic exponent or an amplitude-envelope measurement. The solid segment begins at age four; the dashed infant segment requires a suitable proxy. Step heights and exact ages are illustrative; the falsifiable maturation claim is the order L2→L3→L4.
